title: task8s Scenario Set
description: Schema for task8s scenario set YAML files (v1alpha1). A scenario set is a structured learning exercise consisting of an introduction, one or more scenarios, and optional manifest definitions. The user works through each scenario by answering questions correctly before advancing.

apiVersion.description: Schema version identifier. Must be exactly 'v1alpha1'. Always place this as the first field in the file.

name.description: Display name of the scenario set. Shown in the UI bottom bar while the user works through scenarios.

k8sVersion.description: Kubernetes version string (e.g. '1.32.0'). Required when any manifestDefinition uses autoLoad: true. Used to fetch the JSON Schema for that manifest kind from the kubernetes-json-schema repository.

introduction.description: Page shown between the home screen and the first scenario. Use it to explain the topic, set expectations, and link to external resources.

timing.description: Optional timer configuration. When omitted, no timer is shown.

manifestDefinitions.description: Reusable manifest type definitions. Each entry declares a Kubernetes resource kind that manifest questions can reference by ID. Required when any scenario contains a manifest question.

scenarios.description: Ordered list of scenarios the user works through. Each scenario is a self-contained exercise; the user must answer all questions correctly before advancing to the next.

ExternalLink.description: A labelled hyperlink to an external resource.

url.description: Fully-qualified URL of the external resource.

text.description: Human-readable link label displayed in the UI.

Introduction.description: Introductory content shown before the first scenario. Supports context paragraphs, images, reference links, and visual breaks.

elements.description: Ordered list of introduction elements rendered top-to-bottom.

IntroductionElement.description: One element in the introduction. Must be one of: context, image, references, or break.

IntroContextElement.description: A paragraph of text in the introduction. Supports markdown formatting.

text.description: Paragraph content. Supports markdown: bold, italic, inline code, fenced code blocks, headings, lists, tables, blockquotes, and links.

IntroImageElement.description: An inline image in the introduction.

alt.description: Alternative text for the image, used for accessibility.

IntroReferencesElement.description: A list of labelled external links displayed as a reference block in the introduction.

links.description: One or more external links to show.

IntroBreakElement.description: A visual spacer that adds vertical whitespace between context blocks in the introduction.

Timing.description: Controls the optional timer shown while the user works through scenarios.

enabled.description: Whether to show a timer. Set to true to activate the timer display.

limitSeconds.description: Optional countdown target in seconds. When set, the timer counts down from this value. When omitted (with enabled: true), the timer counts up. The timer never blocks the user even if it reaches zero.

ManifestDefinition.description: Declares a Kubernetes resource kind that manifest questions can reference. Provides the JSON Schema used to validate the user's YAML input. Either autoLoad or an inline schema should be provided; without one, validation will report an error.

id.description: Unique identifier for this definition within the scenario set. Referenced by manifestDefinitionId in manifest questions.

kind.description: Kubernetes resource kind, exactly as it appears in the manifest (e.g. 'Pod', 'Deployment', 'Service'). Case-sensitive.

apiVersion.description: Kubernetes API version string for this resource (e.g. 'v1', 'apps/v1', 'networking.k8s.io/v1'). Must match the apiVersion used in the manifest.

schema.description: Inline JSON Schema object used to validate manifests of this kind. Use this for non-standard or custom resources. For standard Kubernetes resources, prefer autoLoad: true instead.

autoLoad.description: When true, the JSON Schema for this resource kind is automatically fetched from the kubernetes-json-schema repository at runtime using the top-level k8sVersion. Requires k8sVersion to be set. Use for all standard Kubernetes resources (Pod, Deployment, Service, etc.).

SubcommandToken.description: One expected token in the subcommand chain of a command question (e.g. 'get', 'pods'). Tokens are matched in order after the executable.

name.description: Canonical subcommand name (e.g. 'pods'). This is the accepted form used in validation error messages.

aliases.description: Additional accepted spellings for this subcommand token (e.g. ['pod', 'po'] for 'pods'). The user may type any of these.

PositionalSpec.description: Constraint on one positional (non-flag) argument that appears after the subcommand chain. Use index to target a specific argument position when validating multiple positionals.

index.description: Zero-based position among positional tokens (i.e. non-flag arguments after the subcommands). Defaults to 0 when omitted. Specify explicitly for each entry when the command takes multiple positional arguments.

required.description: Whether this positional argument must be present in the user's answer. Defaults to true.

value.description: The positional argument must exactly equal this string.

oneOf.description: The positional argument must equal one of these strings.

regex.description: The positional argument must match this regex pattern (partial match).

description.description: Human-readable label for this argument, used in validation error messages shown to the user (e.g. 'node name', 'pod name').

FlagSpec.description: Constraint on one flag in a command question. Value constraints (value, oneOf, regex) are checked whenever the flag appears, regardless of whether it is required.

name.description: Canonical long-form flag name without leading dashes (e.g. 'namespace' for --namespace). Used in validation error messages.

short.description: Single-character short form without leading dash (e.g. 'n' for -n). The user may supply either the long or short form.

aliases.description: Additional accepted long-form names without leading dashes. Use for flags that have multiple valid names beyond the canonical name.

required.description: Whether the flag must appear in the user's answer. Defaults to false.

boolean.description: When true, the flag takes no value (e.g. --all-namespaces, --force). Defaults to false.

value.description: The flag's value must exactly equal this string when the flag is present.

oneOf.description: The flag's value must equal one of these strings when the flag is present.

regex.description: The flag's value must match this partial regex pattern when the flag is present.

repeatable.description: When true, the flag may appear more than once in the command (e.g. multiple -l label selectors). Defaults to false.

minCount.description: The flag must appear at least this many times. Implies the flag is repeatable.

maxCount.description: The flag must appear at most this many times.

forbidden.description: When true, the flag must not appear in the user's answer at all. Use to prevent the user from bypassing a constraint (e.g. forbidding --all-namespaces when a specific namespace is required).

CommandSpec.description: Describes the expected structure of a kubectl (or other) command. The validator checks that the user's input matches the executable, subcommand chain, positional arguments, and flags defined here. Argument order does not matter.

executable.description: The base command the user must type (e.g. 'kubectl', 'kubeadm', 'helm').

strictness.description: How the validator handles tokens not covered by the spec. 'strict' (default) rejects unknown flags and unexpected positional arguments. 'permissive' allows them — useful when you only want to validate a subset of the command.

subcommands.description: Ordered list of expected subcommand tokens appearing after the executable (e.g. [{name: 'get'}, {name: 'pods', aliases: ['pod', 'po']}]). The count of entries defines the boundary between subcommands and positional arguments.

positionals.description: Constraints on positional (non-flag) arguments that appear after the subcommand chain.

flags.description: Constraints on flags. Only include flags you want to validate — omit flags that the user is free to use or omit without affecting correctness.

ManifestFieldSpec.description: Checks that a specific field in the user's manifest has the expected value. Evaluated after JSON Schema validation passes.

path.description: Path to the field within the manifest. Uses dot notation for nested fields and numeric segments for array indices (e.g. 'metadata.name', 'spec.containers.0.image'). For keys that contain literal dots — such as Kubernetes annotations like 'storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class' — wrap that segment in square brackets: 'metadata.annotations[storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class]'.

expectedValue.description: The value the field must equal. Can be a string, number, or boolean.

BaseQuestion.description: Fields common to all question types.

header.description: The question text shown above the input. States the task or goal. Must not contain the answer or any part of it — plain text only, no markdown.

hint.description: Shown after the user submits a wrong answer for the first time (when hintsEnabled is true on the scenario). Must not contain the answer — point toward the right concept or direction instead. Plain text only, no markdown.

correctAnswerInfo.description: Extra explanation shown inline below the success message after the user answers correctly. Use to add depth or context about why the answer is correct. Shown after the answer is submitted — may reference the answer. Plain text only, no markdown.

cel.description: CEL (Common Expression Language) expression for custom validation logic. For single-line and multiline questions, replaces the expectedAnswer check entirely. For command questions, runs as an additional gate after structural validation passes. For manifest questions, runs alongside expectedFields. The bound variable 'answer' always contains the raw input string. For manifest questions, 'manifest' is also bound to the parsed YAML object, so you can traverse fields (e.g. manifest.metadata.name == 'foo') in addition to string-searching the raw YAML with answer.contains(...). Command questions also expose: executable, subcommands, positionals, flags, unknownFlags, extras.

SingleLineQuestion.description: A single-line text input. The user's answer must exactly match expectedAnswer, or pass the cel expression if provided.

expectedAnswer.description: The exact string the user must type. Ignored when cel is provided.

MultilineQuestion.description: A multi-line textarea input. Behaves identically to single-line but the input accepts newlines. Use for answers that span multiple lines (e.g. two commands, a YAML snippet).

expectedAnswer.description: The exact multi-line string the user must type. Ignored when cel is provided.

CommandQuestion.description: A terminal-style input with a $ prompt. Validates that the user typed the correct executable, subcommands, positional arguments, and flags. Argument order does not matter.

command.description: Specification of the expected command structure.

initialValue.description: Optional text pre-filled in the command input when the question first loads. Use for cloze-style questions where part of the command is given and the user must complete it. The pre-filled portion should establish context (e.g. the subcommand chain), not supply the part being tested.

ManifestQuestion.description: A YAML editor pre-configured for writing a Kubernetes manifest. The user's input is validated against the manifest definition's JSON Schema and any expectedFields checks.

manifestDefinitionId.description: ID of the manifestDefinition entry that describes the expected resource kind. Must match an id in the top-level manifestDefinitions array.

initialContent.description: Optional YAML pre-filled in the editor when the question loads. Use to scaffold the manifest structure (e.g. provide field names with blank values) without giving away the expected values. Omit entirely to require the user to write the manifest from memory.

expectedFields.description: Additional field-level checks run after JSON Schema validation passes. Use to verify specific values the schema alone cannot constrain (e.g. metadata.name must equal 'my-pod').

ChoiceAnswerType.description: Role of a choice in a multiple-choice question. 'Solution': this option alone is a complete correct answer — selecting it succeeds immediately. 'PartOfSolution': this option is one required part of a combined correct answer — all PartOfSolution entries must be selected together and submitted. Cannot be mixed with Solution in the same question. 'Invalid': this option is incorrect — selecting it fails immediately (single-answer mode) or causes submission to fail (combined mode).

Choice.description: One selectable option in a multiple-choice question.

text.description: The label shown on the option button. Plain text only.

description.description: Optional sub-text shown below the choice label to provide additional context. Plain text only.

MultipleChoiceQuestion.description: A question where the user selects from a list of options. Three modes depending on answerType usage: single correct answer (one Solution), any of several (multiple Solutions), or combined answer (all PartOfSolution entries must be selected). Note: multiple-choice tests recognition rather than recall — prefer command, single-line, or manifest questions for Kubernetes practice.

choices.description: List of answer options. Must contain at least two entries. Must include at least one Solution or at least two PartOfSolution entries. Do not mix Solution and PartOfSolution in the same question.

OrderingItem.description: One draggable item in an ordering question.

id.description: Stable internal identifier used in correctOrder to define the correct sequence. Never shown to the user. Use short, descriptive slugs (e.g. 'apply', 'new-rs', 'ready').

text.description: The label displayed on the draggable card. Shown to the user.

OrderingQuestion.description: A drag-and-drop question where the user arranges items into the correct sequence. Items are displayed in a randomised order that is guaranteed not to equal the correct order, so the question is never trivially correct on first view.

items.description: The items the user will drag into order. Must contain at least two entries. Displayed in a randomised sequence on load.

correctOrder.description: Array of item IDs in the correct sequence. Every ID must correspond to an entry in items, and the array length must equal the number of items.

SequenceChildQuestion.description: A step within a sequence question. Supports single-line, multiline, and command steps. Manifest steps are not supported.

SequenceQuestion.description: A multi-step question where each step must be answered correctly before the next is revealed. Treated as a single question element — nothing after the sequence in the element list is shown until all steps are complete. Use only when steps are tightly coupled with no meaningful intermediate feedback; otherwise use separate standalone question elements.

steps.description: Ordered list of child questions. Must contain at least two steps. Supported types: single-line, multiline, command. Each step supports its own header and hint.

header.description: Overall heading shown above all steps. States the overarching task. Plain text only.

hint.description: Shared hint shown after any step fails for the first time (when hintsEnabled is true). Plain text only.

correctAnswerInfo.description: Explanation shown after all steps are completed correctly. Plain text only.

Question.description: A question the user must answer correctly. Must be one of the supported question types: single-line, multiline, command, manifest, sequence, multiple-choice, or ordering.

ContextScenarioElement.description: A paragraph of background text shown in a scenario. Always visible as soon as every question before it in the elements list has been answered. Supports markdown formatting. Use to explain the situation, provide context, or frame the next question — never to reveal the answer.

text.description: Paragraph content. Supports markdown: bold, italic, inline code, fenced code blocks, headings, lists, tables, blockquotes, and links.

QuestionScenarioElement.description: A question the user must answer correctly. Gates all elements that follow it in the list — nothing after this element is shown until the question is answered correctly.

ManifestScenarioElement.description: A read-only syntax-highlighted YAML editor used to display a manifest to the user. This is not a question — the user cannot edit it. Use it to show an example manifest, a resource definition, or the result of a previous step. Place after a manifest question to show the ideal solution once the user answers correctly.

content.description: The YAML content to display in the read-only editor. Shown verbatim with syntax highlighting.

header.description: Optional heading displayed above the editor. Use to frame what the user is looking at. Plain text only.

footer.description: Optional caption displayed below the editor. Use for additional notes or caveats. Plain text only.

TableScenarioElement.description: Tabular data displayed inline in the scenario. Use to simulate kubectl output after a command question, or to show reference data. Place after a command question to show what the output would look like — this makes the scenario feel interactive.

style.description: Rendering style. 'terminal' renders kubectl-style output: monospace font, left-aligned columns, no borders — use after kubectl command questions. 'default' renders a styled HTML table with headers — use for structured reference data. Defaults to 'default'.

columns.description: Column header names. The number of entries determines the expected number of cells per row.

items.description: One row of table data. Must contain exactly one string per column. Use an empty string for empty cells. Quote values containing special characters (slashes, colons, spaces).

rows.description: Table data rows. Each inner array is one row.

ScenarioElement.description: One element in a scenario's element list. Must be one of: context, question, manifest (display), or table. Elements are revealed progressively — an element is visible only when every question before it in the list has been answered correctly.

ExplanationContextElement.description: A paragraph of explanatory text shown in the scenario explanation. Supports markdown formatting.

text.description: Explanatory content. Supports markdown. Use to explain why the answer is correct, what alternatives exist, what can go wrong, and deeper background on the concept.

ExplanationImageElement.description: An inline image shown in the scenario explanation.

alt.description: Alternative text for the image, used for accessibility.

ExplanationReferencesElement.description: A list of labelled external links shown in the scenario explanation. Every explanation should include at least one references element linking to official Kubernetes documentation.

links.description: One or more external links to show.

ExplanationElement.description: One element in a scenario explanation. Must be one of: context, image, or references.

Explanation.description: Shown after all questions in a scenario are answered correctly. Use it to explain why the answers were correct, provide deeper context, and link to official documentation. Every scenario must have an explanation.

elements.description: Ordered list of explanation elements rendered top-to-bottom. Should include at least one context element and one references element.

Scenario.description: A self-contained learning exercise. The user must answer all questions correctly before advancing to the next scenario. Each scenario should focus on a single command, concept, or task.

title.description: Displayed as the scenario heading. Should describe the specific task or concept covered.

category.description: Groups scenarios for completion statistics. Use consistent names across scenarios in the same set (e.g. 'Core Concepts', 'Workloads', 'Networking', 'Storage', 'Security', 'Troubleshooting'). Must not contain < or > characters.

hintsEnabled.description: Whether hints are shown after a wrong answer in this scenario. Defaults to true. Set to false to suppress all hints for a harder experience.

elements.description: Ordered list of context, question, manifest display, and table elements. Elements are revealed progressively: an element is visible only when every question before it in the list has been answered correctly.

explanation.description: Shown after all questions in the scenario are answered correctly.
